title: EvidenceScore: A Composite Trust Metric for Cochrane Meta-Analyses
body: Can a composite trust score reliably grade Cochrane meta-analyses across multiple quality dimensions? We applied five automated detectors to 6,229 meta-analyses from 501 Cochrane systematic reviews, each assessing audit quality, evidence consistency, statistical robustness, prediction stability, and statistical power. A weighted composite combined these dimensions using pre-specified weights of 30%, 20%, 20%, 15%, and 15% respectively, mapping each meta-analysis to a 0-100 trust score and letter grade from A-plus through F. The mean EvidenceScore was 69.0 (SD 9.6, range 35-98), with only 17.4% of meta-analyses achieving grade A or above (score 80 or higher) and 1.9% scoring F below 50. Robustness and stability components were the primary bottlenecks, averaging 43.1 and 41.2 respectively, while audit quality scored highest at 83.3. Most Cochrane meta-analyses achieve moderate trust but fall short of high confidence thresholds. These scores depend entirely on upstream detector accuracy and pre-specified weights that have not been empirically calibrated.
